FiniteGaussianMatrix (whole result)

Formalizes the finite-dimensional part of Section S:compact-gaussian (notes/integrated_compact_gaussian.tex at a284420): Lemma L:gaussian-trace-bounds (lines 47-90), Proposition P:finite-gaussian-matrix (lines 98-177, including the Hermitian core E:finite-hermitian-gaussian, line 150, and the Hermitian dilation, lines 156-169) and Remark R:gaussian-one-variance-test (lines 179-193). It uses two modules: StratonovichHAMSecondMoment/GaussianIBP.lean, a reusable foundation for finite Gaussian integration by parts, and StratonovichHAMSecondMoment/FiniteGaussianMatrix.lean, which contains the three results. L:gaussian-scalar-powers is reused from GaussianScalarPowers (finite Hoelder, the integer-power bound, and E Z^r <= (E Z)^r in the bootstrap). The three results are stated with the manuscript's hypotheses by the wrappers gaussian_trace_bounds_paper, finite_hermitian_gaussian_paper, finite_gaussian_matrix_paper and gaussian_one_variance_test_paper. Nothing is supplied as a hypothesis. The integration by parts E[g_k P(g)] = E[d_k P(g)] and the integrability of polynomial moments (TeX lines 122-126) are proved, not assumed.

Abstractions and why they are faithful. - Gaussians. "Independent real standard Gaussians" are g : Fin N -> Omega -> R on an arbitrary probability space with iIndepFun g P and HasLaw (g k) (gaussianReal 0 1) P for every k. GaussianIBP.map_eq_stdPi shows that their joint law is stdPi N = Measure.pi (fun _ => gaussianReal 0 1). The general theorems are stated on stdPi N and transferred to the probability space through integral_comp_eq_stdPi. - One-dimensional integration by parts comes from Mathlib's whole-line integration by parts and the density identity phi' = -x phi. - N-dimensional integration by parts uses Fubini along Fin.insertNth k. The partial derivative is a hypothesis on every coordinate slice. - Matrices are complex matrices indexed by finite types. - ||A||_{S_p}^p = Tr((A^*A)^m) for p = 2m is schattenPow A m, the real part of that trace. schattenPow_trace proves that the trace is real and nonnegative, so taking the real part loses nothing. ||A||_{S_p} = schattenNorm A m = (schattenPow A m)^(1/(2m)). - |Y| and V^(1/2) are CFC.abs Y and CFC.sqrt V, the continuous functional calculus under MatrixOrder. abs_pow_even and schattenNorm_sqrt give the identities the TeX uses: |Y|^(2j) = Y^(2j) and ||V^(1/2)||_{S_p}^p = Tr V^m. - Real traces. The TeX compares several traces as real numbers. Lean compares their real parts. gaussian_trace_bounds_paper also records that the imaginary parts of its right-hand traces vanish; the other wrappers state real-part bounds only, and the reality of those traces follows from the proved matrix lemmas (trace_psd, trace_mul_pow_im).

Implicit hypotheses made explicit: - the measurability of the Gaussians (inside HasLaw); - the integrability of ||X||_{S_p}^p and of Tr Y^(2m), which is part of each conclusion because the Bochner integral of a non-integrable function is 0 in Lean; - the evenness of p, stated as p = 2m with m >= 1 a natural number.

Every real power has a nonnegative base, so no statement holds through a junk value.

Hypotheses carried but unused: o, n, N >= 1 in finite_gaussian_matrix_paper ([Nonempty o] [Nonempty n] (_hN : 1 <= N)). The general theorem finite_gaussian_matrix_zero also covers the empty family N = 0.

Proof route. The statements are the manuscript's; four steps differ from the TeX route: - The doubly stochastic step diagonalizes D' = U^* D U and applies Jensen's inequality to t^m (convexOn_pow) instead of the tangent-line inequality. - The derivative of t -> Re Tr(B (Y + t B_k)^j) is computed in the type synonym NMat n, matrices with the L-infinity operator norm. This avoids the product-topology diamond on Matrix. Polynomial growth is bounded with the same norm. - The integration by parts is applied to real parts of traces, which are real-valued functions. - The m = 1 case of E:finite-hermitian-gaussian follows from the same integration-by-parts identity with an empty word, where the TeX invokes independence directly.

Not formalized: the infinite-dimensional part of S:compact-gaussian, namely L:cutoff-factorization, P:cutoff-singular-values, P:compact-two-envelopes, L:compact-positive-order, P:localized-finite-variance, C:finite-gaussian-operators and P:cutoff-boundary-tests. These need Schatten classes and singular values of compact operators on Hilbert space, Courant-Fischer, and Sobolev spaces on the torus.

FiniteWick (foundation: the finite Wick formula, used by L:terminal-wick)

A reusable foundation with no manuscript label of its own, proved in full with nothing supplied. It formalizes the Wick (Isserlis) step in the proof of L:terminal-wick (notes/notes_stratonovich_ham_second_moment.tex at a284420): the formula E:terminal-wick-formula (lines 3619-3622) with "each pairing has coefficient one" and "if m+n is odd, the expectation is zero" (line 3638), the Gaussian moment computation of the proof (lines 3662-3675), the moment bound of lines 3651-3656, and the pointwise positivity and comparison of covariance products (lines 3693-3695). The chain integrals themselves are in TerminalWick. Abstractions: a pairing (pair partition) of a finite set S of a linearly ordered finite type is a fixed-point-free involution of S, normalized to the identity off S so that each pair partition is exactly one function (pairings); its weight takes one factor c(a, p a) per pair, at the smaller element a < p a, so every unordered pair contributes once with coefficient one (pairWeight); wickSum c S is the sum of the weights. For S all of Fin (2k) these are the pair partitions Pi_k of the TeX. The double factorial is Nat.doubleFactorial with natural subtraction, so (2*0-1)!! = 0!! = 1, the empty-product convention of line 3639. Gaussian side: stdPi N (from GaussianIBP) is the law of N independent standard Gaussians, and Mathlib defines multivariateGaussian 0 K as the image of the standard Gaussian under x -> sqrt(K) x (CFC.sqrt). CenteredGaussianField W K P states the TeX's hypothesis "centered real Gaussian field with covariance K" (lines 3601-3602) as: for every finite family of points p : Fin n -> X, the matrix (K(p_a, p_b)) is positive semidefinite and (W(p_a))_a has law multivariateGaussian 0 (K(p_a, p_b)). Implicit hypotheses made explicit: K positive semidefinite (otherwise Mathlib's multivariateGaussian 0 K is the Dirac mass at 0), and every integral identity for Gaussian monomials (products of finitely many coordinates or field values) comes with the integrability of its integrand, either as a conjunct or in a separate theorem. The exception is the bridge integral_multivariateGaussian_eq for an arbitrary continuous F: it is an equality of Lean's totalized integrals and assumes no integrability, so for a non-integrable F (for instance exp(x_0^4) under a nondegenerate Gaussian) both sides are the junk value 0; integrability transfers only through the separate equivalence integrable_multivariateGaussian_iff. No hypothesis is carried unused. Proof-route differences: the Gaussian identity is proved by Stein's recursion E[g_e F(g)] = E[partial_e F(g)] (GaussianIBP.integral_coord_mul_eq_of_growth) for x = A g, expanded along the partner of the least index (wickSum_eq_sum_erase), instead of differentiating the moment generating function (lines 3664-3673); the conclusion is the same. The moment bound E(prod_{a<n} W(p_a))^2 <= (2n-1)!! V^n (CenteredGaussianField.sq_moment_le) is the Wick formula for the 2n values together with the count of (2k-1)!! pairings (card_pairings_even, wickSum_abs_le) and |K(x,y)| <= V (CenteredGaussianField.abs_le), instead of Hoelder's inequality and L^(2n) Gaussian moments; the bound is the same. No conclusion is narrower than the TeX step it formalizes. Junk values: wickSum is a finite sum, and every Bochner integral of a Gaussian monomial appears with a proof of integrability; only the continuous-F bridge above can equate two junk values, and the monomial results apply it to integrable monomials. Refutations (refutations/finite-wick/), all combinatorial or one-dimensional controls without junk-value reliance: PairingCount ((2k)!/k! pairings of a 2k-set; k = 2 gives 12, not 3), AbsBound (the pairing-sum bound without (2k-1)!!; c = 1 on Fin 4), NonnegDropped (pairing sums nonnegative for arbitrary real weights, not a covariance; c = -1 on Fin 2) and FourthMoment (E x^4 = 1 for a standard Gaussian x, an actual Gaussian law; the Wick formula gives 3). Not formalized here: everything about the chain measures, the L^2-valued integrals and the series (see TerminalWick). The four route definitions unpair, pairUp, matBound and monoDeriv are public but are not listed as claims; they appear only inside the statements of the auxiliary rows below.

FockForm (narrower result: L:fock-form and L:interval-contractions on the coefficient model of the m multiplied coordinates (coordinates i > m not modelled), symmetry without self-adjoint operator packaging, spatial operators not constructed; spatial column bounds supplied)

Consumers of the Hermite/Fock foundation (GaussianHermite, HermiteFock) in notes/notes_stratonovich_ham_second_moment.tex at a284420 (main TeX; all line numbers in this section refer to that file). Three labelled results and the hypotheses of one audit lemma.

L:fock-form (statement lines 2472-2489, display E:fock-sandwich lines 2484-2488, proof lines 2491-2527). The proof has a spatial half (lines 2492-2513: the representation W_eps = sum_i g_i e_i, Gaussian isometry, spatial Plancherel and E:phase-resolvent of L:phase-contractions, giving sum_i H_i^2 <= R_alpha rho^(alpha-4) for H_i = A_rho^(-1/2) M_(e_i) A_rho^(-1/2), then compression to S_b) and a Fock half (lines 2515-2526). The Fock half and the compression are proved; the bound sum_i H_i^2 <= R_alpha rho^(alpha-4) is the named input FockColumn H (R_alpha rho^(alpha-4)) (column form sum_i ||H_i u||^2 <= c ||u||^2, which is the TeX's quadratic-form inequality). The wrapper fock_form_paper states the lemma with the standing class of S:static-phase (lines 2054-2066) and R = R_alpha (line 2061). Class: inputs supplied.

L:interval-contractions (statement lines 2828-2848, proof lines 2850-2897). E:interval-column (lines 2832-2835), the first display of the lemma, is the named input (FockColumn for the operators A_rho^(-1/2) M_(e_m) with constant R_alpha rho^(alpha-2)). Proved from it: the same column bound for band-compressed multiplications (lines 2875-2878), the phase insertion on a color in its vacuum with norm at most sqrt(R_alpha) rho^((alpha-2)/2) in ||(f,g)||_rho (lines 2838-2841, 2878-2880), the substitution sum (A_rho^(-1/2) M A_rho^(-1/2))^2 <= R_alpha rho^(alpha-4) (lines 2882-2886) and E:interval-fock (lines 2844-2846, 2887-2891). The wrapper interval_contractions_paper assumes H:homog, as the other S:interval-upper wrappers do, and R = R_alpha (line 2820). Class: inputs supplied.

E:occupied-multiplication (lines 1802-1804, inside the proof of P:mild-construction; statement lines 1773-1787, proof from line 1793), for finitely many coordinates: ||HF||_2 <= 2 sqrt(n+1) ||H||_2 ||F||_2 for H = sum_i a_i g_i and F a real polynomial of total degree at most n in independent standard Gaussians g_1, ..., g_m, on stdPi m (occupied_multiplication, squared form) and on a probability space (occupied_multiplication_paper). Nothing is supplied. Narrower than the TeX: F ranges over polynomials in finitely many coordinates and H over their span, not over the closed space P_(<=n) and all centered linear Gaussians; the closure step and the almost-sure identification (lines 1810-1814) are not formalized.

The degree-raising hypotheses of StratonovichHAMAudit.HermiteWord.cut_eq_raw for the concrete Fock model (goodDeg_vac, goodDeg_insert, goodDeg_frame, truncC_eq): coefficient vectors over colors Fin m with one Gaussian mode per color, insertion J_i v = gmul i (K_i v) (multiplication by g_i tensored with an operator K_i on X), frames acting on X, and per-color degree truncation P = truncC Nc. They have exactly the shapes of the hypotheses hv0, hJ, hF, hP of cut_eq_raw (with bump i d = fun c => d c + if c = i then 1 else 0). The application is the audit file StratonovichHAMAudit/HermiteWordFock.lean (section HermiteWordFock (narrower result:L:finite-word-cutofffor one Gaussian mode per color and single finite words; finite sums and Bochner integrals not formalized)), since HermiteWord is not a module.

Model. Spatial L^2 is an abstract complex inner product space X; the operators of the TeX enter as continuous linear maps on X: H_i for A_rho^(-1/2) M_(e_i) A_rho^(-1/2), P for the band projection S_b, S for A_rho^(-1/2), M_i for M_(e_m). The Gaussian factor is HermiteFock's coefficient model (degrees <= N; the truncation P_N is restriction of coefficients) or its expansion iota on stdPi m. Self-adjointness is used in the symmetric form <T u, w> = <u, T w>, derived from IsSelfAdjoint (on a complete X) in the wrappers. The quantifier "uniformly in eps, m, b" is the independence of the constant d_N rho^(alpha/2-2) from eps, m and P, given the supplied column bound.

Implicit hypotheses made explicit. rho > 0 (the TeX writes A_rho = rho^2 - Delta); S_b symmetric and idempotent and commuting with A_rho^(-1/2); ||A_rho^(-1/2) f|| <= rho^(-1) ||f|| (from A_rho >= rho^2).

Hypotheses carried but unused (underscore hypotheses, confirmed by the proofs). fock_form_paper: local finiteness of Gamma and mu, evenness, temperedness, positive definiteness, the spectral relation and the scaling of Gamma, and eps > 0; used are 0 < alpha < 2, the formula for R_alpha (to get R_alpha >= 0 by IntervalScalar.ralpha_nonneg) and rho > 0. interval_contractions_paper: of H:homog only the fields alpha_range, threshold and alpha0_pos are used (for 0 < alpha < 2), and eps > 0 is carried and unused.

Route differences. General coefficient operators H_i replace the TeX's rotated basis (line 1805), and the annihilation part is bounded through the finite adjoint identity (see HermiteFock); for E:occupied-multiplication the case H = 0 needs no separate treatment.

Narrower conclusions and not formalized. In L:fock-form, the Gaussian factor consists of the m multiplied coordinates (coordinates g_i with i > m, on which P_N also acts in the TeX, are not modelled), and symmetry is proved for the sandwiched truncated operator on the coefficient model (the finite coefficient pairing identity; no operator-space packaging as a self-adjoint operator is stated), not for B_(N,m,b) itself. Not formalized: the spatial half of L:fock-form and E:interval-column (supplied), the construction of W_eps, e_i, M_(e_i), A_rho and S_b on spatial L^2, the closure step of E:occupied-multiplication and the rest of P:mild-construction.

Junk values. rho > 0 throughout, so rho^(alpha-4), rho^(alpha-2) and rho^(alpha/2-2) are genuine powers; square roots are of nonnegative reals (R_alpha >= 0 is proved in the wrappers); every integral conclusion includes integrability. fockD N R uses Lean's real square root, 0 for R < 0, which no wrapper reaches.

Refutations (refutations/fock-form/): CompressNonProjection (compression by a symmetric P that is not idempotent can increase the column bound), OccupiedConstant (the constant n+1 in place of 4(n+1) in occupied_multiplication fails for H = F = g, n = 1) and TruncWithoutCutoff (truncC_eq without d <= N fails).

FrequencyRow (whole result)

Formalizes Proposition P:frequency-row (lines 47-139) and Corollary C:frequency-time (lines 141-165) of notes/integrated_wave_variance.tex at a284420 (the file is byte-identical at ba01d98, so the line numbers hold for both revisions). It also formalizes the definitions E:variance-scale-profile (lines 12-20), E:frequency-row-kernel (lines 33-37) and E:frequency-row-integral (lines 38-42), and the closed-ball remark after E:frequency-translated-growth (lines 29-31). bracket and frequencyPair (Q_h of E:masked-frequency-pair) are reused from MaskedTrigProducts. J_h(xi) is a lower Lebesgue integral in [0, inf], the "nonnegative extended integral" of line 43, so no Bochner junk value enters its definition. Nothing is supplied as a hypothesis.

The quantifier order is exactly exists K, forall d nu C h xi. frequency_row proves exists K >= 0, forall d (nu a measure on R^d) C, C >= 0 -> growth -> forall h, 0 < h -> h <= 1 -> sup_xi J_h(xi) <= K C B_alpha(h). It also proves, for each xi, nu-integrability of lambda -> Phi_h(xi, xi-lambda) and the real-integral bound <xi>^(2 gamma) int Phi_h(xi,xi-lambda) nu(dlambda) <= K C B_alpha(h) (the finiteness at lines 136-137). Its hypotheses are a < 1, alpha + a < 2, 2 gamma <= 1 and alpha + 2 gamma < 2. The section's range 0 < gamma < min(1/2, (2-alpha)/2) (E:variance-gamma-range, lines 7-9) implies the last two. frequency_time has the same form, exists K_beta >= 0, forall d nu C h, with the extra hypotheses 2 beta < 2 - a and 2 beta < 3 - a - alpha. The _paper wrappers take the section's hypotheses: H:homog with a = alpha0 as HomogCovariance d alpha a Gamma mu (lines 5-6), the range of gamma, a locally finite (Radon) nu, C >= 0 and the growth bound. The corollary also takes 1/2 < beta < min(1 - a/2, (3-a-alpha)/2) (E:variance-beta-range, lines 143-145). In the wrappers the constant is chosen before d, Gamma, mu, nu, C, h (and xi).

Implicit hypotheses made explicit: B(y,r) in E:frequency-translated-growth is read as the open ball, the weaker hypothesis, and closedBall_le derives the closed-ball bound. nu is a measure on the Borel sigma-algebra. Measurability of the kernel is proved, not assumed. Integrability is part of the conclusion.

Hypotheses carried but unused (wrappers): gamma > 0, beta > 1/2, local finiteness of nu, and all of H:homog except alpha0 < 1 and alpha0 + alpha < 2. The general theorems hold for every d, including d = 0, and every real alpha meeting their numerical hypotheses.

Proof route. The integrand is bounded pointwise by two dyadic shell majorants of closed balls of radius 2^j: one around xi on the near region |lambda| <= 4|xi|, one around 0 on the far region. The TeX splits at 4q, q = max(1,|xi|). On the near region <xi> >= 2^n/5 gives the single ratio 2^(alpha+2gamma-2) < 1 for all three cases of alpha. This replaces the three-case bound on A_xi(q) (lines 60-99). The far region and the bound on S(h) follow lines 101-135, split at the first M with h 2^M > 1, which is L + 1 of line 121. The corollary follows lines 155-163. Rows labelled "no direct label (auxiliary to the Lean proof route)" serve only this route.

Not formalized: the instance nu = mu with C = C_Gamma. It needs P:masked-spectral-growth (integrated_covariance_foundation.tex), which is not in this module. The rest of S:wave-variance (the forms on the full phase, lines 167 onward) is also not formalized, except L:phase-bessel (lines 346-366, module PhaseBessel) and P:wave-two-variances (module WaveTwoVariances, with named inputs; there P:frequency-row is applied at nu = nu_R, C = C_nu).

GaussianComparison (narrower result: only the finite Gaussian comparison of P:masked-noise-completion)

Formalizes the finite Gaussian comparison used in P:masked-noise-completion (Completion on the same noise) of S:masked-covariance (notes/integrated_covariance_foundation.tex at a284420, statement lines 188-206, the comparison sentence lines 201-205; proof lines 208-247, the comparison argument lines 239-246). This is a standalone finite result supporting the label, not the label. For a finite index type iota, real matrices A, B with A and B - A positive semidefinite (A <= B in positive semidefinite order, lines 240-241: b^T A b <= b^T B b for every real b), every seminorm N on R^iota (EuclideanSpace R iota) and every real p >= 1, the moments x -> N(x)^p are integrable against the centered Gaussian laws N(0,A) and N(0,B) (Mathlib's multivariateGaussian) and int N(x)^p dN(0,A) <= int N(x)^p dN(0,B) (line 244, E norm(X)^p <= E norm(X+Z)^p, with the finiteness of lines 245-246). Every norm is a seminorm, so the TeX's "every norm" is covered; the integrability statements are conclusions because a Bochner integral of a non-integrable function is 0.

Outside Lean (D1): the identification of A with the covariance matrix of the masked noise evaluations W(zeta_R F_i) and of B with the auxiliary Gram matrix of N_R (lines 201-203 and 239-240), the inequality E W(zeta_R F)^2 <= N_R(F)^2 behind A <= B (lines 230-231), the noise identity E:masked-actual-noise-norm (lines 190-193), membership of mathcal D in the test-noise completion, the contraction extension and its joint Gaussianity (lines 199-201, 230-237). No hypothesis of the Lean theorems stands for them; they are what a statement about the noise would add.

Proof-route differences. The coupling of lines 242-244 ("diagonalizing B - A constructs a centered Gaussian vector Z ... independent of X, on a product space") is the identity of laws N(0,B) = N(0,A) * N(0,B-A) (multivariateGaussian_conv, by characteristic functions, Measure.ext_of_charFun), and the integral against the convolution is the iterated integral over the product. The conditional Jensen step is Jensen's inequality (ConvexOn.map_integral_le) for the convex function y -> N(x+y)^p and the centered law N(0,B-A), for almost every x. Finite moments come from IsGaussian.memLp_id and N(x) <= C norm(x).

The calibration lemmas coordSeminorm, coordSeminorm_apply and integral_coord_sq (int |x_i|^2 dN(0,S) = S_ii) have no manuscript label and are used by the refutations (refutations/gaussian-comparison/).

GaussianHermite (foundation: normalized Hermite polynomials)

A foundation with no manuscript label of its own; everything is proved and nothing is supplied. The manuscript (notes/notes_stratonovich_ham_second_moment.tex at a284420, main TeX) uses "normalized Hermite polynomials" in three proofs: L:fock-form (lines 2515-2517), the multiplication bound E:occupied-multiplication inside the proof of P:mild-construction (lines 1805-1810) and L:finite-word-cutoff (lines 2556-2558). It uses two facts about them: multiplication by the coordinate g_i acts by g_i h_k = sqrt(k_i+1) h_(k+e_i) + sqrt(k_i) h_(k-e_i), and the h_k are orthonormal under independent standard Gaussians. The TeX takes the creation and annihilation algebra from Janson (cited at lines 2467-2468). This module proves both facts, and the spanning step of E:occupied-multiplication.

Formalized. The probabilists' Hermite polynomials He_n are Mathlib's Polynomial.hermite mapped to real coefficients (hermR, values He). The module proves the Appell property He_(n+1)' = (n+1) He_n (absent from Mathlib), the recurrences, Gaussian integration by parts on polynomials (gE_X_mul, from GaussianIBP.integral_mul_eq_integral_deriv), the shift E[He_(n+1) q] = E[He_n q'], and orthogonality E[He_n He_m] = n! delta_(nm). The normalized h_n = He_n/sqrt(n!) are orthonormal (integral_hn_mul_hn) and satisfy x h_n = sqrt(n+1) h_(n+1) + sqrt(n) h_(n-1) (mul_hn). The products h_k(x) = prod_i h_(k_i)(x_i) on R^m are orthonormal under GaussianIBP.stdPi m, the product of m standard Gaussian laws (integral_hk_mul_hk), and satisfy the coordinate recurrence of the TeX (coord_mul_hk). The spanning step: every real polynomial in x_1, ..., x_m of total degree at most n is a real combination of the h_l with |l| <= n (mvPolynomial_mem_hermiteSpan, via monomial_mem_hermiteSpan and the triangularity pow_mem_span1).

Abstractions. Gaussian coordinates are the coordinate functions on Fin m -> R under stdPi m; the transfer to independent standard Gaussians on a probability space is GaussianIBP.integral_comp_eq_stdPi, used in FockForm.occupied_multiplication_paper. Multi-indices are functions Fin m -> N; k - e_i is pointwise truncated subtraction.

Junk values. None of the statements depends on one: sqrt(n!) > 0, every integral statement comes with its integrability, and k - e_i (or n - 1) only appears multiplied by a coefficient that vanishes exactly when the subtraction truncates: sqrt(k_i) (or sqrt(n)) in the normalized formulas, k_i (or n, as in n * hermR (n - 1)) in the unnormalized ones.

Not formalized here: the closed Gaussian polynomial spaces, infinitely many coordinates, and the Wiener chaos decomposition. Labelling: a row is labelled with a manuscript step only where the TeX states it (the recurrence and the orthonormality of the normalized polynomials, and the spanning step of E:occupied-multiplication, which the TeX uses when it passes to "finite-coordinate polynomials"); the remaining public facts are foundation rows ("no direct label") or route helpers.

Refutations (refutations/gaussian-hermite/, each a Lean proof that a wrong variant is false, with the package statement at the same point): OrthogonalityNoDelta (dropping the Kronecker delta in E[He_n He_m] = n! delta_(nm)), UnnormalizedOrthonormal (E[He_2^2] = 2, so the normalization is needed) and RecurrenceNoLowering (dropping the lowering term of mul_hn).

GaussianScalarPowers (whole result)

Formalizes all four parts of L:gaussian-scalar-powers (notes/integrated_compact_gaussian.tex). In the last part, "E" is the integral against a probability measure, "finite expectation" is integrability, Z >= 0 holds almost everywhere, and the integrability of Z^r is proved as part of the conclusion. Finite Hoelder is proved through Mathlib's inequality rather than the manuscript's normalization; the statement is the manuscript's.

GramScalarAlgebra (whole result)

Formalizes all three parts of L:gram-scalar-algebra (notes/integrated_positive_gram.tex), with C_ij = <k_i, k_j> as in the section's setup. The Hilbert-space statements hold in any real inner product space (completeness is not needed), and the section's other standing assumptions (C_ij >= 0, ell_i > 0, b_i >= 0) are not used by this lemma. gram_scalar_algebra_paper restates all three parts with exactly the manuscript's hypotheses (a real Hilbert space and C_ij >= 0). These overlap the step facts PositiveGram.scalar_sqrt_dual and PositiveGram.gram_norm_square.

H1Density (foundation: density of test functions in H^1)

A deterministic foundation of wave L7 (item L7-c), in StratonovichHAMSecondMoment/H1Density.lean: smooth compactly supported functions are dense in the weak-gradient H^1(R^d; R) of WeakSobolev. It carries no manuscript label of its own. The manuscript states the fact in one sentence in the proof of P:spatial-four-linear (notes/integrated_spatial_occupation.tex at revision a284420, proposition lines 219-237, proof lines 239-298; the density sentence and its sketch are lines 262-266) and uses it to extend smooth-profile statements to H^1 profiles: in the same proof at lines 270-271 ("take smooth approximants converging in H^1") and line 290, and in the proof of P:spatial-energy-map (lines 327-348) at lines 328-330 and 339. Every hypothesis is stated; nothing is supplied. In the completion module SpatialOccupationL7Completed it discharges the density hypothesis hdense of SpatialFourLinear (P:spatial-four-linear and P:spatial-energy-map).

  • The space is the package's own H^1 (Mathlib has no Sobolev spaces): WeakSobolev.IsTestFunction (C_c^infinity(R^d; R)), WeakSobolev.HasWeakGradient f g (int f d_v phi = -int <g, v> phi for every test function phi and direction v) and WeakSobolev.MemH1 (f in L^2 with a weak gradient in L^2); the gradient of a smooth function is the classical field VariationalFloor.grad. The approximation is in the graph norm: norm(phi_n - f)_2 -> 0 and norm(grad phi_n - g)_2 -> 0, which is convergence in the TeX's H^1 norm.
  • H1TestDense d is the predicate (its body is fixed for the consumers of wave L7); h1TestDense d proves it for every d, including d = 0, which is more than the manuscript's d = 1, 2, 3. exists_test_approx is the eps form and h1TestDense_of_memH1 the MemH1 form.
  • hasWeakGradient_of_tendsto is the converse (an L^2 graph limit of test functions has the limit gradient as weak gradient), so the weak-gradient H^1 is the closure of C_c^infinity in the graph norm. The manuscript does not state it; it is used by the refutation DropWeakGradient.
  • Lean proof route (different from the TeX in order and in the mollification step). (1) Mollify first: mollify phi u = rho_phi * u with the normalized bump rho_phi = phi.normed volume; the L^2 contraction eLpNorm_mollify_le (Cauchy-Schwarz against the probability weight, then Tonelli and translation invariance) and the density of continuous compactly supported functions in L^2 give rho_n * u -> u in L^2 when the bump radii tend to 0 (tendsto_mollify), where the TeX invokes L^2 translation continuity; the weak-gradient identity tested against y -> rho_phi(x - y) gives grad(rho_phi * f) = rho_phi * g (grad_mollify). (2) Then cut off the smooth function h = rho * f with chi_n(x) = chi(x/(n+1)), chi = 1 on the closed unit ball and 0 outside the ball of radius 2; the classical product rule (grad_cutoff_mul), dominated convergence (tendsto_cutoff_smul) and norm(h grad chi_n)_2 <= C norm(h)_2/(n+1) (norm_grad_cutoff_le) give tendsto_cutoff_test. This is the cutoff estimate of TeX lines 262-265 with R = n + 1, applied after mollification to a smooth function, so no weak product rule is needed. (3) An eps/2 argument and eps = 1/(k+1) give the sequence. The mollifiers are VariationalFloor.bumpN (so mollify (VariationalFloor.bumpN d n) f is VariationalFloor.moll f n by definition, for real f).
  • Not formalized: the separability remark of the same proof (lines 266-268), and the "common subsequence Lebesgue-a.e." of lines 270-271 (the density gives L^2 convergence only; an a.e.-convergent subsequence is a separate step for the consumer).
  • Junk values: none relied on. In the density statements f and g are in L^2, so the integrals in HasWeakGradient against test functions are genuine; all norms are eLpNorm values in [0, infinity].

Refutations (refutations/h1-density/): DropMemLpF (drop f in L^2: the constant 1 in d = 1, weak gradient 0, is not an L^2 limit of test functions), DropWeakGradient (drop the weak-gradient hypothesis: f = 0, g = prof e_0 in d = 1, via hasWeakGradient_of_tendsto and WeakSobolev.weakGradient_ae_unique), NotTestFunction (every H^1 function a test function: the indicator of the origin in d = 1), and ContractionConstant (the contraction with constant 1/2, refuted at u = VariationalFloor.prof in d = 1 by tendsto_mollify). No junk-value reliance. Lemmas labelled "no direct label (auxiliary to the Lean proof route)" serve only the Lean proofs and are not TeX steps.

HermiteFock (foundation: the finite Gaussian Fock layer)

A foundation with no manuscript label of its own; everything is proved and nothing is supplied. It is the finite Gaussian Fock layer used in notes/notes_stratonovich_ham_second_moment.tex at a284420 (main TeX): the Fock half of the proof of L:fock-form (lines 2515-2526), the Fock sentences of the proof of L:interval-contractions (lines 2887-2891), the phase insertion on a color in its vacuum (lines 2838-2841 and 2878-2880), and the Hermite step of E:occupied-multiplication (lines 1805-1810). The TeX cites Janson (lines 2467-2468) for the creation and annihilation algebra; this module proves what is used.

Model (decision 5 of wave L9). The Gaussian L^2 space with values in a complex inner product space X is represented by coefficient vectors (Fin m -> N) -> X, indexed by multi-indices, restricted to total degree at most N (degLE m N; Supp N v says v vanishes above degree N). The expansion iota N v (x) = sum_(|k| <= N) h_k(x) v_k in the normalized Hermite functions of GaussianHermite links the two pictures: it is an isometry into L^2(stdPi m; X) (integral_norm_sq_iota; stdPi m is the law of m independent standard Gaussians), multiplication by x_i is a_i^* + a_i on coefficients (coord_smul_iota), and sum_i x_i H_i is the field operator fieldOp H (sum_coord_smul_iota). No tensor-product inner product is used: the "other Hilbert factor" of the TeX is X itself, and the spatial operators H_i are continuous linear maps of X. The TeX rotates H/||H|| to a first coordinate (line 1805); the general column form with operators H_i makes that step unnecessary. Convention: Mathlib's inner product is conjugate-linear in the first slot, whereas the TeX's is linear in the first slot (line 2824); every adjoint identity stated here survives the conjugation, and the norm-square and real-part identities are unchanged.

Formalized. The annihilation and creation operators (a_i v)_k = sqrt(k_i+1) v_(k+e_i), (a_i^* v)_k = sqrt(k_i) v_(k-e_i), the number identity sum_i a_i^* a_i = |k|, and the finite adjoint identity between a_i and a_i^*. The creation row from degrees <= N to degrees <= N+1 has norm at most sqrt(N+1) (creRow_bound), attained on u_i = a_i w for w of exact degree N+1 (creRow_attained). For symmetric H_1, ..., H_m with the column bound sum_i ||H_i u||^2 <= c ||u||^2, c >= 0 (hypotheses of these lemmas, not manuscript inputs here), the field operator sum_i (a_i^* + a_i) (x) H_i maps degrees <= N to degrees <= N+1 with norm at most 2 sqrt(N+1) sqrt(c) (fieldOp_bound), the same after truncation to degrees <= N (fieldOp_bound_trunc), the truncated operator is symmetric (fieldOp_symm_trunc), and both bounds hold in Gaussian L^2 with integrability (gaussian_field_bound, gaussian_field_bound_trunc). Vacuum insertion: E||sum_i g_i w_i||^2 = sum_i ||w_i||^2 (vacuum_insertion_isometry).

Route difference. The TeX bounds the annihilation part as the adjoint of the creation part (line 2522); Lean uses the same adjoint relation through the finite identity sum_inner_ann and Cauchy-Schwarz. Its annihilation theorem maps input degrees <= N+1 to output degrees <= N with squared norm at most (N+1) c; the TeX's sqrt(n) (lines 1806-1809) concerns input degrees <= n, so the two operator domains are indexed differently, and the Fock proof says "the same bound after truncation" (lines 2522-2523). Applied to an input already supported through N, the N+1-to-N theorem leaves an unused degree of slack. The constant 4(N+1)c of the sum does not need the sharper value.

Junk values. The truncated subtraction k - e_i occurs only multiplied by sqrt(k_i), which vanishes exactly when it truncates; c >= 0 is a hypothesis where it is used; every integral conclusion includes integrability. Coefficient vectors are arbitrary functions; only their values in degrees <= N (or <= N+1) enter the stated sums.

Not formalized here: the full Gaussian L^2 space, infinitely many coordinates, the closed polynomial spaces and unbounded number operators.

Refutations (refutations/hermite-fock/): CreRowConstant (the constant N in place of N+1 in creRow_bound fails at the vacuum), NumberOrder (|k| + 1 in place of |k| in number_identity) and VacuumSquareOfSum ((sum_i ||w_i||)^2 in place of sum_i ||w_i||^2 in vacuum_insertion_isometry).

HomogHypothesis (whole result)

States Hypothesis H:homog (main TeX file, Section S:model) in full as the predicate HomogCovariance, and restates E:kappa and E:driver-parameters under it. The manuscript's Fourier convention Gamma = int e^(i xi.x) mu(d xi) is written out explicitly rather than through Mathlib's Fourier transform. A Lean measure is nonnegative, and on R^d a locally finite Borel measure is a Radon measure. The proofs of the two restated results use only the numerical part of the hypothesis.

IndexedCone (narrower result: abstract ground family; identification with the physical wave family not formalized)

Formalizes L:raw-block-indexed-cone (notes/integrated_raw_block_lower.tex at a284420, lines 232-335) with its display E:raw-block-positive-product: for 0 < rho < 1/2 there are an integer B >= 1 and omega, eps_op > 0, and c_* = a_* j_*/4 > 0, such that the product lower bound holds for every N >= 1, every omega-adjacent chain in I = [0,1] and every operator family eps_op-close to the block flows. The whole conclusion is proved, including the exact constant c_* = a_* j_*/4. The lemma uses the ground family of S:compact-mean-family (notes/integrated_compact_mean_family.tex, the C16 results), which is not formalized; its outputs are supplied as ONE hypothesis structure GroundFamily F over an arbitrary real normed space F, with these fields (TeX lines at a284420):

  • P, e, ell, lam: the flows P_sigma(t) (line 17, E:compact-F-block), the growing vectors e_sigma and duals ell_sigma (E:compact-F-projection, lines 270-272) and the rates lambda_sigma (P:compact-ground-family, line 48); e0 and obs are the data e_0 and the bounded observable O_phi (S:actual-raw-block-lower, lines 16-17); d0 is the gap d_0 (E:compact-rate-gap).
  • lam_pos: lambda_sigma > 0 on I, a weakening of sqrt(eps) <= lambda_sigma in E:compact-rate-gap (line 51).
  • ell_e, P_Pi, Pi_P: ell_sigma(e_sigma) = 1 and P_sigma(t) Pi_sigma = Pi_sigma P_sigma(t) = e^(lambda_sigma t) Pi_sigma for t >= 0, exactly E:compact-F-eigen (lines 277-281), with Pi_sigma = e_sigma ell_sigma.
  • d0_pos, normalized_complement: d_0 > 0 and, for every 0 < eta < d_0, a C with ||e^(-lambda_sigma t) P_sigma(t) Q_sigma|| <= C e^(-eta t) for all sigma in I and t >= 0, exactly E:compact-normalized-complement (P:compact-F-complement, lines 344-348). d_0 is abstract: its identification with inf_I(lambda_sigma - mu_sigma) is not needed.
  • e_cont, ell_cont: norm continuity of sigma -> e_sigma and sigma -> ell_sigma on I (P:compact-F-projection, lines 275-276). Continuity and uniform boundedness of Pi_sigma, and boundedness of e, ell, are derived (Pi_bounded_continuous), not assumed.
  • margin_ell, margin_obs: 0 < inf_I ell_sigma(e_0) and 0 < inf_I O_phi(e_sigma), exactly E:compact-positive-margins (lines 283-286).

Every field is a displayed conclusion of P:compact-ground-family, P:compact-F-projection or P:compact-F-complement, or a weakening of one, so the structure is no stronger than C16. scalarFamily shows it is satisfiable. The proof is the TeX cone induction (entrance, rebase, full block, terminal) with the TeX's order of constant choices. ConeConstants records constants satisfying relaxed, sufficient versions of the TeX's inequalities (lines 254-281): the margins a, j are any positive lower bounds of ell_sigma(e_0) and O_phi(e_sigma) on I (not necessarily the infima a_*, j_*), C_gap, eta_gap, nu need only be >= 0 (the TeX takes C_gap >= 1, eta_gap > 0, nu > 0), and M_e, M_ell, M_P, H are any nonnegative bounds (the TeX takes max(1, sup)). positive_product_of_constants proves the product bound for any such constants, with c_* = a j/4, and exists_coneConstants constructs them with the TeX's choices where needed (C_gap >= 1, eta_gap = d_0/2, positive nu) and with a = a_* and j = j_*; the starred constants in the final result come from this specialization. Side conditions made explicit: the TeX fixes E_0 = ||e_0|| = 1, whereas Lean allows any ||e_0|| (a generalization); the families are D : N -> R -> (F ->L F) with closeness required only for m <= N and u in [0, B], and nothing else is assumed, as TeX line 249 says. The product D_N(u) D_(N-1)(B)...D_0(B) e_0 is D N u (chainState D B e0 N). The wrapper indexed_cone_paper carries the section's standing hypotheses (a nonzero Gamma satisfying H:homog, lines 4-9) unused: the lemma depends on Gamma only through the ground family, and C16 itself (the spectral theory of -Delta - V_sigma, the wave phase space and its projections) is not formalized, so the link of G to Gamma is by documentation only.

IntervalScalar (proof steps of C:static-interaction and P:interval-coefficients, inputs supplied; E:static-block-series in full)

Formalizes the deterministic scalar, combinatorial and Hilbert-space steps of two results of notes/notes_stratonovich_ham_second_moment.tex at a284420: C:static-interaction (statement lines 2685-2731, proof 2733-2796) and P:interval-coefficients (statement lines 3402-3414, proof 3416-3581). Both results are operator and stochastic statements; every row below is a step row (class inputs supplied, conclusion weaker than the labelled statement), except E:static-block-series, which is a scalar statement and is proved in full with nothing supplied (static_block_series_paper). The operator and stochastic inputs enter as named hypotheses; the last column names each one with its manuscript label.

C:static-interaction. L^2(Omega; X_lambda) is modelled by an arbitrary complete real inner product space E, and the transported phases Y_n = S_0(-h) Z_n^eps(h) by a sequence Y : N -> E; the expectation of an inner product is the inner product of E. This is faithful because the proof of E:static-interaction (lines 2733-2770) uses only the Hilbert structure: the order bounds of lines 2746-2751, the Gaussian parity of line 2752, and the two first-variance bounds of lines 2737-2742. Those are the supplied hypotheses hY0, hY, hodd, hborn, hmean. The identification of I_sigma^eps(h)(f,g) with sum sigma^n Y_n (lines 2687-2692) is not formalized. Lean proves that sum sigma^n Y_n converges and the bound (1 + E(h, sigma, lambda)) N^2. L_alpha, B_alpha, x and E are the definitions staticL, staticB, staticX, staticE, word for word; A stands for A_alpha and may be any constant >= 0. The section's constants are R_alpha = alpha pi mu(B_1)/(2 sin(pi alpha/2)) and D_Gamma of E:phase-constants (lines 2058-2065), for locally finite mu, Gamma on R^3 and 0 < alpha < 2. These are the only clauses of the TeX's covariance class (line 2054) in the wrappers. Evenness, positive definiteness and scaling enter only through the supplied hypotheses. R_alpha >= 0 and D_Gamma >= 0 are derived (ralpha_nonneg, dgamma_nonneg). The _step and static_block_series forms take them as hypotheses. The TeX argues with the absolutely convergent double series; Lean bounds the partial sums, regrouped by r + s = 2k (square_sum_eq), keeps the first coefficient signed, and passes to the limit. For E:independent-static-blocks, Lean proves the scalar iteration and 1 + y <= e^y. The per-block bound m_(j+1) <= e^(lambda h_j)(1 + E) m_j is supplied (lines 2787-2793: it uses E:static-interaction, \|S_0(h_j)\|^2 <= e^(lambda h_j), density and tensoring with the independent past). The operators M_j(h_j) and their L^2 extensions are not formalized. Hypotheses carried but unused: 0 < alpha in static_interaction_step; 0 < alpha in static_block_series (its 0 < alpha0 is used: with alpha + alpha0 < 2 it gives alpha < 2); local finiteness of mu, Gamma (it only makes the ball masses finite, so that toReal is not a junk value); lambda h_j <= 1 in independent_static_blocks_paper.

P:interval-coefficients. The energy coefficient [s^(2k)] E\|U(T;s)v\|^2, the split inner products Q_(r,q) and \|v\|_(1/T)^2 are real numbers coef, Q p, V. Colors are j : Fin M with the TeX's sorted label i = j + 1. Supplied hypotheses: - hsplits: E:interval-energy-splits combined with the reflection parity (lines 3478-3488). - hfixed: L:fixed-split (E:fixed-split-bound; lemma lines 3053-3094) at lambda = k/T. Its per-color factor is splitFactor, with l_i as splitEll. - hinv: L:inventory-product as the proposition InventoryProduct alpha alpha0 C_inv (lines 2986-2998). Proved in InventoryProduct (inventory_product) and discharged in IntervalScalarCompleted, whose *_completed forms do not take it. Lean formalizes the rest of the assembly (lines 3499-3547): the length substitution h_i <= L T/i at lambda = k/T, sigma_i^2 <= c h_i^(-alpha0) (singleton_weight_le, cross_weight_le, higher_weight_le); the split count 2l + 1 <= 3^l; k^2 <= 4^k; the coefficient-of-a-product identity (kvector_sum_eq_coeff); and the reduction L -> max(1, L), c -> max(c, 0) (lines 3417-3420). Together these give the explicit constant C = 12 max(c,0) max(1,L)^beta C_split C_inv. The paper wrapper assumes R_alpha > 0 and sigma_i > 0, the hypotheses of L:fixed-split, so that hfixed is literally that lemma. Neither is used in the proof. The TeX's zero-noise case and the sign reduction (sigma_i, W_i) -> (|sigma_i|, sgn(sigma_i) W_i) (lines 3417, 3420-3423) change the Gaussian fields and are not formalized, so the conclusion is narrower there. Positive lengths h_i > 0 are explicit (the TeX writes h_i^(-alpha0)). The identification of the coefficients with the finite-interval model is not formalized: the Hermite cutoff (lines 3490-3497; the lemma L:finite-word-cutoff it invokes is proved in HermiteWordFock only with one Gaussian coordinate per color) and the paragraph "Identification and summation" (lines 3549-3566). For E:interval-phase-bound (lines 3567-3579), Lean proves summability of the coefficient series and the bound e exp(nu C^(1/nu) R_alpha^(1/nu) T^(beta/nu)) V, the TeX's display with its absorbed constant nu C^(1/nu), from four supplied hypotheses: - the power-series identity at s = 1; - vanishing odd coefficients; - the zero-order bound e V; - the coefficient bound. Both wrappers state the section's class as H:homog (HomogCovariance d alpha alpha0 Gamma mu, line 225; the section's standing class at lines 2814-2819 is that of H:homog), from which 0 < alpha < 2, 0 < alpha0 < 1 and alpha + alpha0 < 2 are derived (homog_alpha_range); the other clauses are carried and not used.

Junk values: in the manuscript-facing bounds every real power has a positive base, or is (k!)^nu, or is i^q with i >= 1 (or a nonnegative base with a positive exponent where monotonicity is used), and every denominator satisfies the stated positivity conditions. The unrestricted definitions (invV, invB, invCoeff) and the bridge identities of IntervalScalarCompleted (stated for all k, i) also include Lean's totalized zero-index values, which no bound uses. R_alpha and D_Gamma use ENNReal.toReal of ball masses, finite under local finiteness. Summability is proved, never assumed through tsum.

IntervalScalarCompleted (narrower result: positive-noise scalar coefficient assembly of P:interval-coefficients; identification with the interval evolution and the zero and sign reduction not formalized; analytic inputs supplied)

Integration module of wave L7 for Section S:interval-upper of notes/notes_stratonovich_ham_second_moment.tex (at a284420), in StratonovichHAMSecondMoment/IntervalScalarCompleted.lean. It discharges the one cross-item input of IntervalScalar: the hypothesis hinv : IntervalScalar.InventoryProduct alpha alpha0 C_inv, which states E:inventory-product of L:inventory-product (lines 2986-2997), and which InventoryProduct.inventory_product (wave L7-a) proves in full. The two modules write the same statement differently, and the bridge is proved here, not assumed:

  • invV_eq, invB_eq, invCoeff_eq: the coefficient functions agree (invV = vCoef, invB = bCoef, invCoeff = factorCoeff); InventoryProduct writes beta = 4 - alpha - alpha0, p = 2 - alpha0 and nu = 3 - alpha through TypeContinuity.betaOf, InventoryProduct.pOf and TypeContinuity.nuOf.
  • prod_fin_eq_inventoryProduct: the product over j : Fin M at i = j + 1 used by IntervalScalar is InventoryProduct.inventoryProduct, the product over i in Finset.Icc 1 M.
  • inventoryProduct_holds: under 0 < alpha0 < 1 and alpha0 + alpha < 2 (the hypotheses of inventory_product), IntervalScalar.InventoryProduct alpha alpha0 C with C = InventoryProduct.inventoryConst alpha alpha0 = 4 e^(K(alpha, alpha0)); inventoryProduct_holds_paper gives the same, with C > 0, under H:homog (lines 225-242), of which only alpha0_pos, alpha0_lt_one and threshold are used.
  • interval_coefficient_assembly_completed, interval_coefficient_assembly_paper_completed: the two IntervalScalar theorems that take hinv (interval_coefficient_assembly and interval_coefficient_assembly_paper, step rows of P:interval-coefficients, E:interval-coefficient-bound, lines 3405-3408), re-issued without hinv and with C_inv = inventoryConst alpha alpha0. Every other hypothesis is kept exactly; each proof is one application of the source theorem.

No other IntervalScalar theorem takes hinv. InventoryProduct (whole result)

Formalizes L:inventory-product (A coefficient bound for a product with nonnegative coefficients; notes/notes_stratonovich_ham_second_moment.tex, main file, at a284420: statement lines 2986-2998 with E:inventory-product at lines 2994-2997, proof lines 3000-3040) in full. Nothing is supplied as a hypothesis. The exponents are those fixed by the section S:interval-upper (line 2804) at lines 2811-2812: nu = 3 - alpha (TypeContinuity.nuOf), beta = 4 - alpha - alpha0 (TypeContinuity.betaOf) and p = 2 - alpha0 (pOf). The object is the actual coefficient: v_i and b_{i,l} (lines 2989-2991) are vCoef and bCoef word for word, the ith factor 1 + v_i z + sum_{l>=2} b_{i,l} z^l is the Mathlib formal power series factorSeries (PowerSeries.mk), the product over i = 1, ..., M is inventoryProduct (a product over Finset.Icc 1 M), and [z^k] is PowerSeries.coeff k. The TeX's "finite C = C(alpha, alpha0), independent of M, k" is the explicit real inventoryConst alpha alpha0 = 4 e^(K(alpha, alpha0)) (K = expConst), which is fixed before M and k are quantified and depends on nothing else (not on d, Gamma, mu). inventory_product is the general form: for 0 < alpha0 < 1 and alpha0 + alpha < 2 (any real alpha), every M and every k >= 1, [z^k] prod_{i=1}^M (...) <= C^k/(k!)^nu. inventory_product_paper states it under the section's standing hypothesis H:homog (lines 225-242; HomogHypothesis.HomogCovariance d alpha alpha0 Gamma mu) and adds 0 < C. Only the fields alpha0_pos, alpha0_lt_one and threshold are used (through params: nu >= 1, nu <= beta, beta > 2, p > 1, nu + alpha - 2 = 1); the other fields of H:homog are carried and not used. The TeX's k >= 1 is a hypothesis of every theorem that needs it; M ranges over all naturals (M = 0 gives the empty product). Implicit facts made explicit: the evaluation bound [z^k]F <= F(z)/z^k (coeff_prod_le_prod_tsum) carries the summability of each factor at z as a hypothesis, and inventory_product_eval_le proves that summability at z = theta k^nu, theta = 1/4; the tail sums sum_{i>a} i^(-s) <= a^(1-s)/(s-1) (sum_rpow_tail_le, by Mathlib's sum-integral comparison) and sum_{i>=1} i^(-s) <= s/(s-1) (sum_rpow_pos_le), used in the TeX without proof, are proved. Proof-route differences (the statement is unchanged): the factors 1 + Q_i, Q_i = theta k i^(-p), are bounded by e^(Q_i) with sum_i Q_i <= theta k p/(p-1), instead of the TeX's comparison with int_0^inf log(1 + A x^(-p)) dx, which gives C k^(1/p) (lines 3004-3011); both give the C k the proof needs, and no improper integral is used. The uniform bound sum_{l>=2} P^l (1+ly)^2/(l!)^nu <= C P^2 (1+y^2) for 0 <= P <= 1/4, y >= 0 (lines 3029-3030, stated without argument) is proved inside factor_large with C = 128, via (1+ly)^2 <= 2 l^2 (1+y^2), l^2 <= 2^(l+1) and (l!)^nu >= 1; for i <= k (factor_small) Lean assumes the singleton is at most 4P where the TeX says 2P_i, which is weaker and suffices for the S_nu(4P_i) bound. S_nu(x) <= e^(nu x^(1/nu)) is SeriesType.seriesNu_summable_le. Every factor bound is first proved for each partial sum (factor_partial_le) and then passed to the series sum. Junk values: all real powers have positive bases (i >= 1, k >= 1, l! >= 1) and k^(-1) occurs only with k >= 1 in every evaluation and coefficient bound (the unrestricted definitions and factorCoeff_nonneg also cover zero indices with Lean's conventions, used by no bound), and every tsum (factorEval) comes with its summability, so no junk value enters a conclusion. Nothing in the lemma is left unformalized, and no conclusion is narrower than the TeX's. The use of the lemma in the proof of P:interval-coefficients (lines 3537, 3546) is not part of this section (see IntervalScalar; IntervalScalarCompleted connects inventory_product to the input hinv of that proof).

Registered model choice: M1 (the d = 3 wave Green measure via volume.toSphere; its identification with surface measure is not proved; see Scope).

L:low-alpha-convolution (Low-alpha convolution bound) of notes/notes_stratonovich_ham_second_moment.tex at a284420, in StratonovichHAMSecondMoment/LowAlphaConvolution.lean: statement at lines 4702-4716 (displays E:low-alpha-radial, lines 4704-4708, and E:low-alpha-convolution, lines 4710-4714), proof at lines 4718-4757, standing assumptions of the subsection at lines 4691-4700 (H:homog with d in {1,2,3}, the lemma taking 0 < alpha < 1).

Objects (TeX notation of lines 4695-4698). V = mu({norm(xi) <= 1}) is specV mu (the closed unit ball, as in the TeX; SpectralMassIdentity.ralpha uses the open ball for R_alpha, a different constant). min{h, norm(xi)^(-1)} is lowKernel h, with value h at xi = 0, not Lean's min h 0^(-1) = 0. p_eps is the centered Gaussian density with covariance eps I (heatDens eps; the TeX fixes this normalization at lines 4513-4515 and 5004-5005, not inside the lemma), gamma_eps = p_eps * Gamma is gammaEps Gamma eps (a Bochner integral against the measure Gamma; not PhaseContractions.gammaEps, which is p_(2eps) * Gamma, the Gamma_eps of S:static-phase; each module follows its section's notation), and G_{h,eta} = p_eta * G_h is smoothedGreen G h eta = gaussKernel eta * G h (DampedMultiplier.gaussKernel eta = N(0, eta I)); for eta = 0 it is G_h (smoothedGreen_zero), so the TeX's convention G_{h,0} = G_h is a theorem. G_h is WaveGreen.waveGreen d h in the wrappers (the d = 3 sphere measure being the toSphere definitional choice of WaveGreen, Le's decision 4) and any family G in the general theorem.

Formalized. measure_closedBall_eq (first display of E:low-alpha-radial, from mu(cA) = c^alpha mu(A)); integral_lowKernel (V < infinity, integrability and the layer-cake identity, as in the TeX); the Fourier Fubini step that the TeX invokes at lines 4736-4738 without displaying it (gammaEps_spectral, an identity of Lean integrals under the bare predicate IsSpectralMeasure Gamma mu with no integrability conclusion; and smoothed_pairing_spectral for every finite measure G, under tempered Gamma, mu, with the integrability of both integrands and of p_eps(x - .) against Gamma as conclusions; smoothedGreen_pairing_spectral for G_{h,eta} under GreenFourier); gammaEps_nonneg and abs_waveHat_le_lowKernel (the bounds of lines 4747-4753); and the whole lemma low_alpha_convolution, for every d and every family G with GreenFourier G: E:low-alpha-radial and, for all eps > 0, eta >= 0, z, the integrability of y -> gamma_eps(y + z) against G_{h,eta} and E:low-alpha-convolution. The uniformity of line 4715 is the order of quantifiers (the bound does not depend on eps, eta, z).

Wrappers. low_alpha_convolution_paper: under H:homog (HomogCovariance d alpha alpha0 Gamma mu, d in {1,2,3}, no Gamma != 0), alpha < 1 (so 0 < alpha, returned as the first conjunct) and the supplied GreenFourier (waveGreen d). low_alpha_convolution_one: the same in d = 1 with nothing supplied (DampedMultiplier.greenFourier_one). After wave L9 the input is discharged in every dimension by L9Completed.low_alpha_convolution_paper_completed (section L9Completed), with WaveGreenFourier.greenFourier.

Supplied input (one, discharged in L9Completed): GreenFourier (waveGreen d) (G_h finite and charFun (G_h) = waveHat h, i.e. G_h hat(xi) = sin(h norm(xi))/norm(xi) with value h at 0, for h > 0). It is exactly the identity the TeX imports from the source at lines 4738-4744, with the finiteness of G_h that the same display states (G_h(R^d) = h); it is no stronger than the TeX's input.

Hypotheses made explicit. The general theorem assumes Gamma and mu tempered, mu locally finite, IsSpectralMeasure Gamma mu and SpectralHomogeneous mu alpha (from H:homog by MaskedSpectralGrowth.spectralHomogeneous_of_homog). Integrability is proved where the principal statements use it: integrable_heatDens (the inner integrand p_eps(x - .) against tempered Gamma, eps > 0), smoothed_pairing_spectral (both integrands, as conjuncts), and the wrappers low_alpha_convolution, low_alpha_convolution_paper, low_alpha_convolution_one and L9Completed.low_alpha_convolution_paper_completed (every integral of their conclusions). The auxiliary gammaEps_spectral (an equality of Lean integrals under IsSpectralMeasure Gamma mu alone) and gammaEps_nonneg (nonnegativity for any Gamma) have no integrability conclusion; V < infinity is proved, so V.toReal is not junk; 1 - alpha > 0. Fields of H:homog used by the wrappers (directly or through spectralHomogeneous_of_homog, as recorded in the module): mu_radon, mu_tempered, Gamma_tempered, spectral, scaling, alpha_range; carried, unused: dim (used only by the L9Completed wrapper, to discharge the input), alpha0_pos, alpha0_lt_one, Gamma_radon, Gamma_even, Gamma_posdef, mu_even, threshold.

Integrability of e^(-eps norm(xi)^2/2) against mu comes from temperedness (TeX: polynomial ball growth, line 4736). gamma_eps >= 0 because Gamma is a positive measure and p_eps >= 0 (the TeX argues by distributional nonnegativity, lines 4752-4753; the covariance of H:homog is a measure). The upper bound follows the TeX (lines 4744-4750) via smoothed_pairing_spectral, DampedMultiplier.charFun_gaussKernel_conv and WaveKernel.abs_waveHat_le_min.

MaskedAuxiliaryNorm (narrower result: P:masked-auxiliary-norm for complex H only)

Formalizes P:masked-auxiliary-norm (Auxiliary mask norm) of S:masked-covariance (notes/integrated_covariance_foundation.tex at a284420: statement lines 88-100 with the displays E:masked-auxiliary-growth (lines 90-92) and E:masked-hilbert-fourier (lines 95-98), proof lines 102-137), together with the setup of lines 79-86 (zeta_R, k_R, L, and E:masked-auxiliary-measure at lines 83-86). Nothing is supplied as a hypothesis.

Conventions. The section's unitary Fourier transform (lines 8-12), f-hat(xi) = c_d int e^(-i xi.x) f(x) dx with c_d = (2 pi)^(-d/2), is defined directly as paperHat (for f with values in any complex normed space; the integral is a Bochner integral over Lebesgue measure on R^d = EuclideanSpace R (Fin d)), with cd the constant. It is not Mathlib's 𝓕 (kernel e^(-2 pi i <v,w>)); paperHat_eq_fourier relates the two (f-hat(xi) = c_d 𝓕 f(xi/(2 pi))), and paper_inversion is Fourier inversion in the paper's convention. For a Schwartz map the defining integrand is integrable (integrable_paperHat_integrand), so the transforms in the statements are not junk values. zetaR, kR and Lz are the manuscript's zeta_R(x) = zeta(x/R), k_R = zeta_R-hat and L = norm(zeta-hat)_1; zeta is a real Schwartz map (SchwartzMap (Rd d) R), and zeta_R F is x -> (zeta_R(x) : C) • F(x). The density rho_R(eta) = c_d^2 L int norm(k_R(xi-eta)) mu(dxi) is rho, a lower ([0, inf]-valued) integral of a nonnegative function, which is the manuscript's integral without a junk value; nu is volume.withDensity rho. "Radon" is IsLocallyFiniteMeasure (as in HomogHypothesis.HomogCovariance; on R^d a locally finite Borel measure is Radon), "even" and "tempered" are the package's IsEven and IsTempered. C_Gamma is MaskedSpectralGrowth.CGamma, built from the Bochner integral M_Gamma = int e^(-norm(x)^2/4) Gamma(dx); it is the manuscript's constant when Gamma is tempered, as under H:homog (MGamma_pos). In the general forms, which do not assume Gamma tempered, CGamma is that Bochner integral as written.

Statements. masked_auxiliary_norm_paper assumes the section's standing assumptions (lines 5-6) H:homog (HomogCovariance d alpha alpha0 Gamma mu) and Gamma != 0 (a = alpha0 plays no role in this proposition), a real Schwartz zeta != 0 (line 79), and a separable complex Hilbert space H with an H-valued Schwartz map F (lines 93-94). It proves: zeta-hat is integrable and L > 0; and for every R > 0: k_R is integrable with norm(k_R)_1 = L, nu_R is even, tempered and locally finite, nu_R(B(y,r)) <= c_d^2 L^2 C_Gamma r^alpha for open and closed balls, all y and r > 0, with a right side that does not depend on R; and E:masked-hilbert-fourier: norm((zeta_R F)-hat)^2 is mu-integrable, norm(F-hat)^2 is nu_R-integrable, the inequality holds both for lower integrals and for Bochner integrals, and the right side is finite (proof lines 134-135). It uses the H:homog fields mu_radon (only to make mu s-finite), mu_tempered, mu_even, spectral and scaling; the other fields, Gamma != 0, the inner product and the separability of H are carried but unused. The general form masked_auxiliary_norm assumes only: mu s-finite, tempered and even, IsSpectralMeasure Gamma mu, SpectralHomogeneous Gamma (d - alpha), zeta != 0, and E any complex Banach space. The pieces carry their own hypotheses, stated in their rows.

Implicit hypotheses made explicit: mu s-finite for the Tonelli steps (derived from mu_radon in the wrapper); integrability of every integrand whose Bochner integral is stated; measurability is proved, not assumed; the balls are Metric.ball y r and Metric.closedBall y r.

Proof route (differences from the TeX): - L > 0 (stated without proof at line 82) is proved by Fourier injectivity (eq_zero_of_paperHat_eq_zero, from paper_inversion). - The ball bound follows the TeX: Tonelli and the substitution u = xi - eta (nu_apply, the display of lines 108-111), then MaskedSpectralGrowth.closedBall_le at every center y + u (mu_closedBall_le) and norm(k_R)_1 = L. - Radon: local finiteness is derived from the ball bound, not from the continuity of rho_R (lines 103-106). - Tempered: Peetre's inequality (1+norm eta)^(-N) <= (1+norm xi)^(-N) (1+norm(xi-eta))^N and the Schwartz decay of k_R give int (1+norm eta)^(-N) dnu_R <= c_d^2 L (int (1+norm xi)^(-N) dmu)(int (1+norm u)^N norm(k_R(u)) du) with the exponent N of mu (lintegral_weight_nu_le); this replaces the "same dyadic argument" of lines 113-114. - Even: k_R(-u) = conj k_R(u) (zeta real) and the evenness of mu, as in lines 106-107. - The convolution identity (zeta_R F)-hat(xi) = c_d int k_R(xi-eta) F-hat(eta) deta (lines 116-120) is proved for a Banach-space-valued F directly by Fourier inversion of F and one Bochner Fubini swap (paperHat_mask); the scalar, finite-rank and projection steps of lines 121-127 are not needed. - Weighted Cauchy-Schwarz (lines 127-128) is proved from the nonnegativity of t -> int a (g - t)^2 (sq_integral_mul_le); the final Tonelli step (lines 133-134) is lintegral_nu.

Narrower than the TeX, or not formalized: - The last sentence of the proposition, "For a real H, the same assertion holds after complexification" (line 99), is not formalized (Mathlib has no complexification of a real Hilbert space). This is the only part of the statement that is missing. - The proof-internal claims that rho_R(eta) is finite at every eta and that rho_R is continuous (lines 103-106) are not formalized; they are not part of the statement, and the Lean route does not need them (rho is [0, inf]-valued and local finiteness of nu_R comes from the ball bound). - The wrapper is not instantiated in Lean at a nonzero Gamma satisfying all of H:homog.

Refutations (refutations/masked-auxiliary-norm/): - PeetreFactor: Peetre's inequality without the factor (1+norm(xi-eta))^N is false (d = 1, N = 1). - CdConvention: c_d (2 pi)^d = 1 (the normalization without the square) is false at d = 2. - KernelNormScaling: norm(k_R)_1 = R^d L (which would lose the uniformity in R) is false for the Gaussian zeta, d = 1, R = 2. - ZetaNonzero: L > 0 without zeta != 0 is false (zeta = 0).

The definitions dil, hatS, zc and zetaS (the dilation, the transform of a Schwartz map as a Schwartz map, and the complex Schwartz forms of zeta and zeta_R) only serve the proof route and have no rows.

MaskedContinuousWave (whole result)

Formalizes L:masked-continuous-wave (notes/integrated_covariance_foundation.tex at a284420, statement lines 378-390, display E:masked-continuous-wave lines 385-389, proof lines 392-423) with the standing assumptions of its subsection (lines 296-298) and the hypotheses T > 0, 0 < a < 1 of L:masked-time-completion (lines 141-156). The factors are c_r(t) = cos(rt) (cFn) and b_r(t) = <r> sin(rt)/r for r > 0, b_0(t) = t (bFn; lines 379-383). Wave and Wave.eval give the choices F_r in {c_r, b_r}, G_rho in {c_rho, b_rho} (line 384). waveFn I F G r rho is 1_I F_r G_rho with real values viewed in C. C_1 is 4 * 3^(1-a) * C_0(a) (line 388), with C_0(a) = 16/(1-a) from MaskedTrigProducts.

What is stated. The manuscript's left side is the norm of the complexified temporal completion H_a^C (lines 297-298). As in MaskedModulation.masked_trig_products_bridged_paper, this norm is modelled abstractly. E is a complex inner product space. V is a submodule of R -> C, the functions accepted into the completion. emb : V -> E is a linear inclusion, and ||f||_a is ||emb f||. H_a is not built in this module. The wrapper masked_continuous_wave_paper takes the manuscript's hypotheses: 0 < a < 1, T > 0, 0 < h <= 1, 0 <= s, s + h <= T, r, rho >= 0, F, G in {c, b}. It also takes the same two supplied inputs as masked_trig_products_bridged_paper, under the same names. hmem says that for every A that is C^1 on I = [s, s+h] (ContDiffOn R 1 A I) and every real omega, 1_I A e^(i omega t) lies in V. This is B24's hmem quantified over every amplitude B24 accepts. Its source is L:masked-time-completion, lines 154-155: bounded measurable amplitudes on a subinterval, extended by zero, belong to the completion. A function that is C^1 on the compact I is bounded there and measurable after extension by zero, so the input asks for no more than its source. hnorm is B24's hnorm verbatim: for f in V with f in L^2(0,T), ||emb f||^2 = Re timeForm a T f f. This is the complexification clause of L:masked-time-completion (lines 153-154, with lines 148-149 and 177-179). The conclusion has two parts. First, 1_I F_r G_rho lies in V. Second, for that element, ||emb(1_I F_r G_rho)||^2 <= C_1(a) (1+T)^4 h^(2-a) Q_h(r,rho), which is E:masked-continuous-wave with the manuscript's constant. No Gamma != 0 is assumed, and the TeX states none.

Implicit side conditions made explicit. The functions are real-valued and enter V through the coercion R -> C. bFn r is also defined for r < 0, but that value is never used, because r, rho >= 0 are hypotheses. No sSup occurs in the statement. In the proof, M and D are suprema over the nonempty set I (since h > 0) of bounded sets, so they are not Lean's junk value. C_0(a) is the junk-free 16/(1-a) because a < 1, and the brackets raised to real powers are at least 1.

Hypotheses carried but unused: T > 0. It follows from 0 <= s, h > 0 and s + h <= T.

The proof route differs from the TeX's; the statement and constant are the same. The TeX first writes b_r = t <r> int_0^1 cos(vrt) dv for r <= 1 (lines 393-398). It then forms H_a-valued Bochner averages over up to two copies of [0,1] and applies Hilbert Jensen (lines 398-407). Next it applies L:masked-trig-products with A(t) = t^j (lines 409-411) and compares brackets (lines 411-419). Lean uses no averaging and no continuity of a parameter family in H_a. Each factor is split into an amplitude, a trigonometric shape and a frequency (amp, trig, fr, eval_eq):

  • c_r = 1 * cos(r t);
  • for r >= 1, b_r = (<r>/r) sin(r t), where <r>/r <= sqrt 2 is the TeX's coefficient (line 393);
  • for r < 1, including r = 0, b_r = b_r * cos(0 t).

masked_trig_products_bridged_paper is then applied once. The amplitude is amp F r * amp G rho and the frequencies are r' in {r, 0}, rho' in {rho, 0}, with |r - r'|, |rho - rho'| <= 1 (waveFn_eq_prodFn, fr_spec). Each factor has an envelope with M_i + h D_i <= sqrt 2 (1+T) (amp_bound, from bFn_bounds). amp_prod_sup bounds the suprema with csSup_le and derivWithin on Icc through uniqueDiffOn_Icc. Together they give M + hD <= 2(1+T)^2, so (M+hD)^2 <= 4(1+T)^4. The TeX instead has (M+hD)^2 <= (1+T)^4 and then the squared scalar coefficient 4. The bracket comparison is the TeX's: bracket_add_le, then bracket_rpow_shift_le, then frequencyPair_shift_le. Together they give Q_h(r',rho') <= 3^(1-a) Q_h(r,rho). The case split is at r < 1 versus r >= 1 instead of the TeX's r <= 1 versus r >= 1; the two differ only at r = 1, where both apply.

Narrower conclusion: none in the statement. This wrapper takes hmem and hnorm for abstract V, emb; MaskedContinuousWaveCompleted.masked_continuous_wave_completed_paper discharges both in the concrete H_a of TimeCompletion (see "TimeCompletion (whole result)"), so L:masked-continuous-wave holds with nothing supplied.

Not formalized: the TeX's averaging argument, because Lean proves the same bound by the route above.

MaskedModulation (whole result)

Covers two modules, TimeSchur and MaskedModulation, on notes/integrated_covariance_foundation.tex at a284420 (the file is identical at ba01d98, so every label and line number below holds at both). It formalizes the Schur bound E:masked-time-schur (lines 150-152, inside L:masked-time-completion, lines 141-156) and L:masked-temporal-modulation (lines 300-309, display E:masked-temporal-modulation at 303-307), both in double-integral form. It also re-issues L:masked-trig-products (lines 347-374) with one supplied input replaced by a narrower one. Both remaining inputs are discharged in TimeCompletion (see "TimeCompletion (whole result)").

What is stated. The manuscript's left sides are norms in the temporal completion H_a and its complexification H_a^C. This module does not use the completion. It is built separately in TimeCompletion, where emb_norm_sq_eq_timeForm identifies the norm with the double integral bounded here. On real compact smooth tests, ||f||_a^2 is by definition the double integral int_0^T int_0^T f(t) f(s) |t-s|^(-a) dt ds (lines 143-145). By lines 153-154 and 177-179, the complexified norm of every f in L^2(0,T) is the same double integral with f(t) conj f(s). Lean bounds exactly these double integrals: TimeSchur.timeForm a T f g is the iterated integral over [0,T]^2 of f(t) conj g(s) |t-s|^(-a), and TimeSchur.kern a x = |x|^(-a).

E:masked-time-schur. time_schur_paper covers real f in L^2(0,T) under the hypotheses 0 < a < 1 and T > 0. It proves that the integrand is integrable on [0,T]^2 and that the double integral is at most (2T^(1-a)/(1-a)) int f^2. time_schur_complex gives the same bound for |timeForm a T f f| with complex f (the complexified form, lines 175-177). The proof is the TeX's: the row integral is at most 2T^(1-a)/(1-a) (lines 171-172; Lean computes it exactly in integral_row), then 2|xy| <= x^2 + y^2 and Tonelli.

L:masked-temporal-modulation. masked_temporal_modulation_paper takes the standing assumptions of lines 296-298 and of L:masked-time-completion (T > 0, 0 < a < 1, I = [s, s+h] inside [0,T], 0 < h <= 1) and the lemma's hypotheses (A is C^1 on I, M = sup_I |A|, D = sup_I |A'|). For every real omega, with F = 1_I A e^(i omega t), it proves two things: the integrand F(t) conj F(u) |t-u|^(-a) is integrable on [0,T]^2, and |timeForm a T F F| <= C0(a) h^(2-a) (M+hD)^2 <h omega>^(a-1) with C0(a) = 16/(1-a). This bounds the absolute value of the complex double integral, which implies the bound on its real part. The constant depends only on a, which is the stated uniformity in T, s, h, A, omega (line 308).

The proof route differs from the TeX's; only the statement and the constant C0(a) match. The TeX differentiates c(v) at the moving endpoint (lines 312-318), splits the square into two conjugate triangles (lines 318-324), treats |omega h| <= 1 directly (lines 326-329), integrates by parts on [1/k, 1] for k = |omega h| > 1, and closes with 8 sqrt 2 <= 16 (lines 331-345). Lean proceeds as follows:

  • c is acorr Phi v = int_R Phi(u+v) conj Phi(u) du with Phi = 1_I A. For 0 <= v <= h this is the TeX's c(v); that identification is not itself a Lean statement.
  • No derivative of c is used. acorr_bound proves |c(v)| <= M^2 (h-v)_+, which contains the TeX's c(h) = 0 and |c| <= hM^2. acorr_lip proves |c(v) - c(w)| <= (M^2 + hMD)(w - v), the integrated form of the TeX's |c'| <= M^2 + hMD.
  • A shear substitution and Fubini (timeForm_eq_acorr) give timeForm = int_R |v|^(-a) e^(i omega v) c(v) dv. The symmetry c(-v) = conj c(v) (integral_acorr_split) writes this as X + conj X, with X the integral over v > 0.
  • Case <h omega> <= 8 (it contains the TeX's case |omega h| <= 1): crude_bound with constant_small.
  • Case <h omega> > 8, so k = h|omega| > 7: the integration by parts is replaced by a half-period shift v -> v + pi/|omega| (osc_bound, with the explicit majorant majorant). The final check is 4 pi 8/7 <= 16 (constant_large).

L:masked-trig-products with the narrowed input. masked_trig_products_bridged_paper has exactly the hypotheses of MaskedTrigProducts.masked_trig_products_paper, except that the supplied modulation bound hmod is replaced by hnorm. hnorm says: for f in V with f in L^2(0,T), ||emb f||^2 = Re timeForm a T f f. This is the complexification clause of L:masked-time-completion (lines 153-154, extended to L^2(0,T) by lines 148-149 and 177-179). hnorm is required only on V intersected with L^2(0,T). The wrapper derives hmod from hnorm and masked_temporal_modulation_paper, using memLp_modeFn to put the modes in L^2(0,T). hmem (the modes lie in V and emb is linear, lines 154-155) stays supplied. The wrapper is stated for abstract V, emb; it says nothing about elements of V outside L^2(0,T). TimeCompletion.masked_trig_products_completed_paper instantiates it with H_a, discharging hmem and hnorm. MaskedTrigProducts itself is unchanged; its masked_trig_products_paper still takes hmod.

Implicit hypotheses made explicit:

  • L^2(0,T) is MemLp f 2 (volume.restrict (Icc 0 T)).
  • A is a function on the reals, and only its values on I enter.
  • C^1(I; C) is ContDiffOn R 1 A I, and A' is derivWithin A I.
  • M and D are sSup over I. envelope_of_contDiffOn uses compactness to show the sets are bounded, so neither is Lean's junk value.
  • Integrability on the product measure is a conjunct of every double-integral conclusion, so the Bochner integrals are not Lean's junk 0.
  • The diagonal value of kern enters only on a null set.

Hypotheses carried but unused:

  • 0 < a in time_schur_paper and time_schur_complex; the general time_schur_rclike needs only a < 1 and 0 <= T.
  • T > 0 and h <= 1 in masked_temporal_modulation_paper and in the bridged wrapper.

The completion H_a and the other clauses of L:masked-time-completion are formalized in TimeCompletion (see "TimeCompletion (whole result)"), not in this module.
